correctness.rationale: Every deleted read creates at most one adjacency overlap defect; a single defect can be bridged if and only if the two remaining read words share their ell-2 overlap, and the parent is unique. If no defect, the retained read path uniquely spells a length-(n-1) word. Its two boundary extensions supply 2q parents except for a single intersection in the constant case, while interior read reinsertion exactly duplicates a symbol in a constant stretch of ell-1 symbols; each eligible strict internal run contributes one distinct parent. The exact defect count follows by an injective source-to-received map for each unique gap and exclusion of constant ell-symbol blocks. A run-composition geometric series supplies the complete rational enumerator, and a length budget proves the sharp maximum. A standalone all-sources finite checker corroborated the formulas in 49 parameter combinations with 343337 feasible outputs and 631205 source/output incidences. Finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

This theorem gives the complete positive-list distribution, exact feasibility count, and sharp worst-case list size simultaneously for every alphabet size, read width, and source length in its domain. The dependence on internal constant-run lengths reveals structure not provided by generic code-redundancy bounds; these exact quantities can inform adversarial list-decoding guarantees and finite-length ambiguity analyses. No claim about code optimality or practical performance beyond these invariants is made.
